name: Insufficient PBKDF2 iteration count (PBEKeySpec)
attack_scenario: An attacker who exfiltrates the password-hash store runs an offline dictionary/brute-force attack; at 1000 iterations a commodity GPU tests billions of candidate passwords cheaply, recovering user passwords in minutes to hours instead of the years a 600k work-factor would impose.
negative_test_hint: run an offline dictionary attack starting with "password123" against an exfiltrated hash and assert cracking is impractical because the iteration count is at least 600000

exemplar.explanation: NIST SP 800-132, the OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet, and BSI TR-02102-1 require a high PBKDF2 iteration count (OWASP recommends 600,000 for PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256); an iteration count below 10,000 offers negligible work-factor against modern GPU/ASIC cracking. A high iteration count makes every guess expensive, turning offline cracking of an exfiltrated hash store from minutes into years.
